gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AV Access KD-E10's '100 W laptop charging' only works when you plug your laptop's own charger into the dock, because its included adapter is 12 V / 3 A (36 W) and just runs the dock. The iDock M10, which is also labelled '100 W', ships with a 20 V / 6 A (120 W) adapter and sends power to the laptop over its included dual-head cable.
standout_why: Cited rivals: racksandwatts.com gives the iDock C10 as 'up to 60 W' and doesn't say where the power comes from. The tesmart.com 2026 guide gives the HDC203-PM24 as '100W PD' and doesn't say whether that is supplied or pass-through. Neither covers the KD-E10, M10, T722 or HDC202. Uncited top results: theofficejournal.com says only 'verify the wattage'. byrdpilot.com is the only one that explains pass-through charging, and it does so only for the IOGEAR GCS1602CC ('with your own charger'), not for any of our candidates. So other sites have the idea, but nobody has applied it to these products. Our own current page also lists both AV Access docks as plain '100 W'.
decides: For a Windows-laptop shopper choosing between the two AV Access docks, the KD-E10 ($169.99) is not a one-cable dock. You still need the laptop's charger at the desk, plugged into the KD-E10. The iDock M10 ($289.99) powers the laptop from its own 120 W adapter. On a Mac the KD-E10 also mirrors its two screens. So the M10 is the one-cable pick, and the KD-E10 is the budget pick only if you keep the laptop charger on the desk. The charging column should be split into 'dock-supplied W' and 'pass-through W', with a footnote.

findings.label: Laptop charging, normalised
findings.value: Up to 100 W pass-through; needs the laptop's own charger plugged into the dock
findings.note: Quotes from the page: 'When connected to a power adapter, the USB C port delivers up to 100W of power' and 'When charging your laptop, please additionally use your laptop's original adapter.' The page doesn't say how much reaches the laptop after the dock's own draw.

findings.label: Included power adapter
findings.value: DC 12 V / 3 A (36 W), for the dock only
findings.note: 12 V × 3 A = 36 W. That cannot supply 100 W, which is why the 100 W figure depends on a second charger.
